name: Harold Woodbury Parsons
bio: The last and latest of the Lewes House circle - 'among the latter-day group of Ned's boys and. the most audacious and elusive, and certainly the least likeable' (Sox). Born plain Harold Parsons at Lynn, Massachusetts (he claimed 1883 and a Harvard degree; the birth certificate says 13 July 1882, and he took 'Woodbury' from his brother's name), he was raised by his 'indulgent Woodbury grandfather' on Commonwealth Avenue, Boston. Warren, consulted at a Boston dinner, advised the art-life abroad: from 1906 Parsons studied in Cassel and Dresden, then made Lewes House his English headquarters 'eight months at a time'. Marshall 'came to despise' him. After Warren's and Marshall's deaths he carried the collecting tradition on as European purchasing agent for Cleveland, Kansas City and Omaha, and ended as a celebrated exposer of forgeries - the 'Etruscan' warriors among them - from his base in Rome, where, after a long life 'despite several attempts at suicide', he died in 1968.
bio_sources: Born: 'The birth certificate of Harold Parsons (no middle name) from Lynn says he was born on 13 July 1882, the son of Edward P. and Marcia E. bio_note: Sox gives the death only as the year (1968, in Rome). The forgery-exposure career (Dossena catalogue with Pico Cellini, 1955, p. 124; the Metropolitan's Etruscan warriors, pp. 117ff; Time magazine plate, 24 Feb. 1961, PDF 244 caption) was read at text layer only - pointers, not verified in the source. NULL FINDING for a parsons--warren romantic edge: Sox's characterizations are mentor-protégé and patronage throughout the pages read ('Ned's boys', 'one of Ned's new friends', 'in obvious emulation of Ned Warren'); no romantic or sexual wording anywhere. Parsons's own gloss of Warren: 'a belated Greek who seemed to live in the age of Pericles and not to belong to the modern world' (p. 221, text layer - pointer).
